title: KHOU 11 Visits ELARA, With Older Adults at the Center
summary: A community-center interview highlighted why listening to people's reactions is part of robot design, not just outreach.

sources.label: Read Chorong Park's original LinkedIn post
University of Houston report on ELARA's community research

paragraphs.text: KHOU 11 visited the Mamie George Community Center to hear about ELARA's companion robot research and meet older adults taking part. Chorong Park shared the September 3, 2026, interview with reporter Amanda Henderson as a behind-the-scenes look at the work.

For Park, the most meaningful part was listening. Participants' questions and reactions help the team understand what feels welcoming, useful, confusing, or intrusive when a robot enters an everyday setting.

Kelly Schafler's University of Houston reporting describes older adults working with students to evaluate existing robots and model ideas for future designs. Their input is helping inform a new robot still in development.

That makes community engagement part of the research itself, not simply a way to explain it afterward. Park's goal is assistance that supports choice and connection without replacing human relationships.

She thanked community members, students, and collaborators for shaping the work. At the time of the post, the television segment was expected near the end of September; the update documented filming ahead of that planned coverage.
